text: Dynamic regulation takes issue with the broad scope of contractual incompleteness and delayed decision-making assumed by the incomplete contract model, contesting the view that such incompleteness and delay are always necessary.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Evolution of Law Dynamic Regulation in a New Institutional Economics Framework (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2267560

isBasedOn.name: Evolution of Law Dynamic Regulation in a New Institutional Economics Framework

abstract: By expanding Kreps's model of organizational culture and applying it to the rulemaking process, dynamic regulation also takes issue with the broad scope of contractual incompleteness and delayed decision-making in the incomplete contract model.
